Galileo Galilei first proposed the concept of inertia. By observing the motion of objects on an inclined plane Galileo deduced that objects move with a constant spéed when no force acts on them.
Galileo published a series of essays named: De Motu (Meaning: "On Motion")
Galileo's first book: La Bilancetta ("The Little Balance") published in 1586.
Newton formulated the three laws of motion.
1st Law of Motion > Law of Inertia
The Law of Inertia states that "An object at rest remains at rest and an object in motion remains in motion at constant velocity unless acted upon by an external force".
Types of Inertia 1. Inertia of Rest: This is the tendency of an object to remain at rest unless acted upon by an external force.
E.g. The dry leaves and fruits falls when we shake a tree.

2. Inertia of Motion: This is the tendency of an object to continue moving in a straight line at a constant speed unless acted upon by an external force. E.g. A person sitting in a moving car may be pushed forward when the car stops abruptly as our legs are in contact with the surface.

3. Inertia of Direction: This is the tendency of an object to continue moving in the same direction unless acted upon by an external force. E.g. When a car makes a sharp turn, your body tends to move in the direction it was previously moving, rather than following the car's. new direction.
Inertia: The tendency of an object to resist changes in its state of motion. It depends on the mass of the object.
